question: What is the growth plan for Frontline?
html:
Frontline growth plan

Frontline is already national, so the plan focuses on three things: earning more per law firm, moving down-market, and going international. The plan runs in four overlapping phases over about 42 months. All financials are estimates, because EBITDA growth has to carry the return on a deal bought at about 12-15x (est.) (Frontline growth plan).

Starting point and capital

  • BSP closed on Dec 9, 2024. The deal was funded with $136.95M of equity from BSP-FL LP and a $90M NXT/Audax term loan. Carlyle AlpInvest added $12.5M directly (Frontline public filings).
  • Adjusted EBITDA at close was about $16-20M (est.), on 2025 revenue of about $100-140M (est.). These are derived from leverage and headcount, not company disclosures (Frontline public filings).
  • Frontline serves about half the AM Law 200 and 900+ law-firm clients (Frontline growth plan).

Four phases

  • Phase 1 (months 0-12): AI service desk and attach. HELIX becomes a product-led service desk with a Tier-0 AI agent. The phase also adds a cyber-posture subscription and legal-AI enablement. ILTA finds 68% of firms have Copilot but only 8% have deployed it firm-wide (Frontline growth plan).
  • Phase 2 (months 6-18): mid-market law firms. The screen covers 143 mid-size firms (17,042 attorneys) across 16 metros. Thirty-seven of them score 65+. The top three are Weber Gallagher (85), Evans & Dixon (83) and Rivkin Radler (82) (Mid-size law firms).
  • The phase also includes tuck-ins of local legal MSPs. Kraft Kennedy is about $21.5M revenue (est.) and Innovative Computing Systems about $12.6M (est.). Both figures are ZoomInfo estimates and directional only (Frontline and Thomas Scientific add-on targets).
  • Phase 3 (months 12-30): eBilling and AR. Client-side AI has pushed invoice rejections from 11% to 18%. The phase consolidates eBilling and AR through targets such as Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group. It also runs four finance agents priced on days-to-pay (Frontline growth plan).
  • Phase 4 (months 24-42): UK and Canada. Entry is through acquired local providers such as Quiss, Accurate Legal Billing and CG Technologies (Frontline growth plan).

KPI roadmap (est.)

MonthRevenueEBITDAMarginHeadcountClients
0$130M$20M~15.4%1,150900
12$150M$25M~16.7%1,3001,000
24$180M$32M~17.8%1,5001,150
36$215M$41M~19%1,6501,300

These figures assume about 9-10% organic growth and about $55M of cumulative acquired revenue by month 36 (Frontline growth plan).

Key risks

  • Every financial figure inherits low-to-medium confidence (Frontline public filings).
  • Revolver, delayed-draw or incremental debt capacity is undisclosed. That capacity governs how fast the M&A phases can be funded.
  • The mid-size firm universe was not drawn from NLJ or Law360 rankings, so the screen is not exhaustive (Mid-size law firms).

Next actions

  1. Replace the modelled baseline with management's actual revenue, EBITDA and margin by service line. Then re-base the KPI roadmap.
  2. Confirm current debt capacity, including revolver, delayed-draw and incremental terms, with NXT and Audax before sequencing the Phase 2 and Phase 3 add-ons.
  3. Validate revenue and ownership for Kraft Kennedy, Innovative Computing Systems and Helm360 beyond the ZoomInfo estimates.
  4. Set Phase 1 baseline metrics with the CEO, Tim Britt: Tier-0 deflection rate and cyber-subscription attach rate.
